## Context

Follow-up accepted by Chris (2026-08-24, option (a)) as the closure for the KNOWN BOUNDARY documented in T-01M0122WMF8EJTB7ERHTEG8HMJ / PR #577 (bypassed-mutation audit). #577 shipped the audit that records a signed ticket-mutation entry for every store mutation from that change forward, and refuses keyless bypass writes. It leaves ONE historical-state gap, documented in code at packages/tickets/lib/trust-root.mjs ("KNOWN BOUNDARY") and adjudicated across review rounds 23/27: a repo whose LAST railed ticket was removed by the PRE-#577 writer has no rail in the ticket set, nothing in the archive, and no manifest marker — so the new predicate reads it as a repo that never used rails, and a later mutation there goes unaudited.

This gap CANNOT be closed inside #577: the evidence does not exist to read (the old writer recorded nothing), and git archaeology over .adlc/tickets on every mutation fails outside a checkout and is too slow for a per-write predicate. It is historical-only and cannot grow — every removal from #577 forward leaves the marker. Accepted as a bounded residual for 1.11.0; this ticket closes it properly.

## What to build

Implement the adoption-record mechanism specified in .adlc/specs/manifest-key-hermeticity.md: a one-time, signed "rails-adoption" record a repo writes when it first upgrades to the audited writer, capturing whether it currently declares (or has ever declared) rails. Once that record exists, the audit predicate reads it instead of inferring rail history from present state, so a subsequent removal of the last railed ticket is still recognized as a railed-repo mutation and audited. Define the bootstrap path for a repo that upgrades WITH rails already present (write the adoption record on first mutation under the new writer), and the path for one that adopts rails later.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A repo that had its last railed ticket removed by the pre-#577 writer, then writes the adoption record, has subsequent mutations correctly audited (the boundary case from #577 rounds 23/27 no longer goes unaudited). verify: a test reproduces the #577 boundary fixture, applies the adoption record, and asserts the next bypassed mutation is refused/audited; `node --test packages/tickets/test/*.test.mjs` exits 0.
2. The adoption record is signed and its absence fails closed (a repo with rails present but no adoption record does not silently read as never-railed once this ships). verify: negative test in the same suite.
3. The KNOWN BOUNDARY comment in packages/tickets/lib/trust-root.mjs is removed and replaced with a reference to the shipped mechanism. verify: `grep -c 'KNOWN BOUNDARY' packages/tickets/lib/trust-root.mjs` returns 0.
4. .adlc/specs/manifest-key-hermeticity.md's adoption-record section is marked implemented. verify: reviewer confirms the spec and code agree.
5. Full suite green incl. the windows ticket-store-platform matrix. verify: `npm test` exits 0.
title: Close the WMF historical-state audit boundary: build the adoption-record mechanism so pre-fix rail removals are detectable
